newsitem.title: USA: Arizona growers sue USDA on wheat fungus.
newsitem.headline: Arizona growers sue USDA on wheat fungus.

text.p: Arizona farm groups have sued the U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman over USDA's battle against the Karnal bunt wheat fungus, a lawyer for the plaintiffs said Friday.

The lawsuit, filed this week in U.S. District Court in Phoenix, seeks to provide plaintiffs some relief from USDA's restrictions. Plaintiffs listed in the lawsuit include the Arizona Wheat Growers Association, Arizona Cotton Growers Association and the Arizona Farm Bureau Federation.

Karnal bunt, a fungus that damages wheat quality and yields but is not known to endanger human health, was discovered in March in parts of Arizona, Texas, New Mexico and California. USDA subsequently mounted restrictions on wheat movement in those areas out of fear of infecting the rest of the U.S. wheat crop.
The groups filing the lawsuit said the restrictions are unfair and threaten to ruin Arizona's $100 million wheat industry.
